stream_log.reasoning: Week of 2026-08-10 to 08-17. Russia-Ukraine produced a rare, publicized Ukrainian battlefield reversal: Kyiv completed its eight-month Oleksandrivka-axis counteroffensive (Jan 29-Aug 12), retaking ~745 sq km and 26 settlements and clearing Russia from nearly all of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast (~10,000 Russian troops killed per Zelenskyy), even as Russia intensified nightly combined strikes (12+ killed Aug 10-11, KN-23 North Korean missiles battle-tested) - this, plus the fresh 86-11 US Senate sanctions package and the Kremlin barring the anti-war Yabloko party from the September Duma elections, nudges russia_stability 0.25->0.24. On the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, Iran and Oman formalized a shipping-route agreement (announced Aug 15), the clearest de-escalation milestone since the June ceasefire collapsed - lifting middle_east_stability 0.15->0.16 and easing nuclear_risk_level 0.33->0.32 - but full reopening still hinges on the US lifting its blockade and sanctions (Araghchi: the Oman deal 'wouldn't translate into the strait's reopening'), and ship attacks continued, so the moves stay small and this remains a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node rather than a new one. Macro turned benign-to-positive: the S&P 500 hit records (clearing 7,800 for a third straight weekly gain) on softer-than-expected July CPI/PPI and an expected Fed hold, shrugging off Brent's climb to ~$87, so global_gdp_growth_modifier ticks 1.02->1.03. Colombia's magnitude-7.4 quake (Aug 10) - its strongest this century, 132+ dead and rising with heavy damage in Pereira - drags latin_america_stability 0.40->0.38. Sustained high-intensity Ukraine combat (the culminating Dnipropetrovsk fighting and continued deep strikes) plus residual Gulf/Red Sea attacks lift cumulative conflict_deaths 1,519,000->1,522,000. Excluded/watched: no new node - the Iran-Oman deal is not a consummated US-Iran ceasefire (blockade holds) and Ukraine's gains are an operational success within the ongoing 2022_russia_ukraine war, not an era-defining discrete event; frontier-AI releases stayed incremental (Qwen3.8, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Gemini 3.6 Flash) after late-July flagships already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick; China-Taiwan pressure held roughly stable with no discrete single-week trigger; supply_chain_resilience held at 0.47 because the Hormuz strait did not actually reopen and oil ticked up on a large US crude stockpile build; and Cyclone Dolphin (China, 1M+ evacuated), Philippines/Sri Lanka monsoon flooding, Canadian (BC) wildfires and the ongoing DRC Ebola PHEIC were regionally acute but map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude this week.

Week of 2026-08-17 to 08-24. Last week's Hormuz optimism collapsed: the 60-day US-Iran memorandum of understanding expired Aug 17 and Trump ruled out extending the ceasefire, declared no talks were underway (Aug 18), threatened to 'bomb the shit out of' Oman if it obstructed reopening the strait, and posted a 'New US Territory' image claiming 'total control' of Hormuz, while a senior Iranian official said Tehran would shift to a 'fully offensive' posture and mount a 'timely and precise' attack to break the US naval blockade (a carrier group was en route to replace USS Lincoln; the UAE detected a missile threat Aug 18). The Iran-Oman shipping framework announced last week did NOT translate into any reopening - Iran's preconditions (lift the blockade, withdraw US forces, permanently end the war) remain unmet and the blockade held all week. Markets re-priced the escalation: Brent surged ~6% to ~$94 (a second straight ~6% weekly gain, fully reversing the prior week's -7% relief rally), Houthis struck another Saudi vessel in the Red Sea, and Israel ramped up strikes on Lebanon and hit the Abu al-Duhur airbase in Syria. This reverses last week's tentative improvements: middle_east_stability 0.16->0.14 (deal collapsed, MOU expired, offensive threats, Lebanon/Syria widening - though Pezeshkian's Aug 21 signal that Tehran wants the war to end soon keeps the slip contained), nuclear_risk_level 0.32->0.34 (MOU lapse, 'fully offensive' threat, carrier surge and UAE missile scare), and supply_chain_resilience 0.47->0.45 (Brent back to ~$94, strait firmly not reopening, blockade entrenched). Macro turned mildly risk-off: the S&P 500 fell ~1.4% on the week to ~2% below its record as the Philadelphia semiconductor index dropped ~5% on rising Treasury yields, Fed-independence worries ahead of Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address, and the renewed oil bid - so global_gdp_growth_modifier eases 1.03->1.02, partially unwinding last week's tick. Russia-Ukraine ground on at high tempo (mutual missile/drone barrages killing civilians; Russian strikes have damaged 300+ Ukrainian fuel stations over six months) with only limited diplomacy - Moscow said it is 'ready for new ideas' but only ones matching Putin's existing goals - so two-front combat lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,522,000->1,525,000 while russia_stability holds at 0.24 (the grind and the tentative Russian openness roughly offset, no decisive single-week mover). Excluded/watched: no new node - the Hormuz re-escalation is a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node, not a discrete era-defining event; Trump's 'very positive' outreach to Kim Jong-un and the scaled-down US-South Korea exercises are a minor Korea de-escalation with no clean structural dimension and are offset by the Iran nuclear-risk move; frontier-AI activity stayed incremental (GPT-5.6 Sol/Luna updates, Claude Sonnet 5 pricing made permanent, Grok Imagine Image 2.0, Meta Muse Spark) after late-July flagships already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick; and the Indonesia M7.7 Flores earthquake (~70 dead) and record Japan/South Korea rainfall predate this window (Aug 13-14) and map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude.

Week of 2026-08-24 to 08-31. The 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis cooled from an acute military standoff into an economic/sanctions confrontation: the US has not struck Iranian targets since late July and Trump canceled a planned attack citing progress in ceasefire negotiations, Iran's and Oman's foreign ministers met Aug 25 to firm up the shipping-corridor understanding, and crude flows through Hormuz recovered to ~6-8M bbl/day, so Brent fell ~5% on the week to ~$89-90 (from ~$94). This eases middle_east_stability 0.14->0.15, nuclear_risk_level 0.34->0.33, and supply_chain_resilience 0.45->0.47 - moves kept small because the blockade nominally holds, Iran still calls the strait 'closed' with its preconditions unmet, and tankers were still hit this week (the LNG carrier Gaslog Shanghai and another vessel near Oman). Markets recovered on the oil relief and a strong Nvidia earnings beat (S&P 500 back to ~7,731, Nasdaq +1.6% on the day, PMI 51.0 still expansionary), lifting global_gdp_growth_modifier 1.02->1.03 and partially unwinding last week's risk-off tick. Russia-Ukraine ran at record intensity: Zelensky said Russia fired ~2,000 attack drones, 1,600+ glide bombs and 31 missiles (including North Korean ballistic) in one week, an Aug 29 strike on a warehouse west of Kyiv killed 38 with several missing, and Russia's MoD signaled a renewed winter energy-infrastructure campaign - lifting cumulative conflict_deaths 1,525,000->1,529,000. Ukraine's deep-strike campaign escalated onto Russia's export economy - drone attacks suspended all three major grain terminals at Novorossiysk (cutting August Russian grain exports by an estimated 0.7-1.2M tonnes, potentially below 2M vs 5.7M a year ago) alongside a Leningrad Oblast oil refinery and a Krasnodar airbase - nudging russia_stability 0.24->0.23. That Black Sea disruption, atop Northern-Hemisphere drought that cut European wheat an estimated 8-10M tonnes, drove wheat +12% on the week to its highest since Feb 2023 (+54% YTD, with corn also at multi-year highs), so food_security_index eases 0.72->0.71 - the first genuine structural food-supply signal in the stream. Excluded/watched: no new node - the Hormuz de-escalation is a shift within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node, not a signed ceasefire or discrete era-defining event, and the grain shock is a development within the ongoing 2022_russia_ukraine war; the US-Venezuela oil-access framework and a Dominican Republic-Venezuela diplomatic thaw are geopolitically notable but not a clean structural mover on latin_america_stability this week; frontier-AI activity stayed incremental (Alibaba Qwen 3.8-Max at 2.4T params, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GPT-5.6 Luna, Meta Muse Spark, plus a first AI-piloted F-16 test flight) after late-July flagships already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick; and South Korea's record 42.5C heat maps to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude this week.

Week of 2026-08-31 to 09-07. August's cooling of the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis reversed sharply into the most serious escalation in weeks: a weekend exchange broke a month of relative calm, Iran laid sea mines in Hormuz and fired missiles at a US base in Jordan, the US cleared the lane and struck Iranian targets (Sep 1) while hitting three Iranian oil tankers, Iran fired ballistic missiles at US aircraft carriers near the strait ('calculated escalation') and struck tankers, and Saudi oil tankers were hit. Brent surged ~8% on the week to ~$95. This reverses last week's tentative improvements: middle_east_stability 0.15->0.13 (month of calm broken, carriers directly targeted, Saudi tankers hit), nuclear_risk_level 0.33->0.35 (fresh US strikes, Iranian ballistic missiles at US carriers, mines in Hormuz), and supply_chain_resilience 0.47->0.45 (chokepoint re-disrupted, tanker war, Brent back near cycle highs). global_gdp_growth_modifier eases 1.03->1.02, partially unwinding last week's oil-relief tick as that relief fully reversed - though equities were resilient (S&P 500 +0.09% on the week to ~7,719, buoyed by a strong 162k August jobs print vs 53k expected), so only a small downtick. Russia-Ukraine ran at high intensity - Russia's jet-powered drones (harder to intercept) killed dozens, ~12 killed Sep 1, heavy fighting in Kostiantynivka, and Zelenskyy warned Putin may conscript 300,000+ - lifting cumulative conflict_deaths 1,529,000->1,532,500 (Ukraine front plus the intensified US-Iran/Gulf tanker war). Watched but not scored: the week's biggest positive geopolitical development was the first serious Ukraine peace push in eight months - US envoys Witkoff and Kushner met Putin in Moscow (Sep 5, three hours, called 'substantive, constructive, exceptionally candid') then Zelenskyy in Kyiv (Sep 6) with a Trump proposal to end the war, and both sides briefly paused aerial attacks on capitals over the weekend - but it produced no signed ceasefire and the war continued at record tempo, so russia_stability holds at 0.23 (the diplomatic off-ramp and the ongoing grind/conscription plan roughly offset, no decisive single-week mover) and no new node is warranted yet; a signed ceasefire would warrant one. Also excluded: the densest 72 hours of frontier-AI releases of the year (OpenAI GPT-6 Astra - first model to trip a critical-cyber safeguard threshold, Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1, Google Gemini 3.8 Flash + Cyber, Meta Muse Spark 1.3, three shipping gated autonomous-cyber tiers) is a notable capability convergence but consistent with the established incremental cadence and does not warrant another integer ai_development_year_offset tick two months after the 4->5 move, nor a discrete node; Germany's AfD regional-election surge, the Argentina-UK Falklands oil dispute, the Sudan aid-convoy airstrike, and the Dutch central bank relocating gold reserves to London on 'geopolitical unrest' are geopolitically notable but not clean structural movers at meaningful magnitude this week; and the season's major typhoons (Ragasa et al.) fall later in September, outside this window. The Hormuz re-escalation is a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node, not a new discrete event, so no new nodes.

Week of 2026-09-07 to 09-14. The defining event was the sharpest NATO-Russia spillover of the war: on Sep 10 Russia sent ~two dozen drones into Polish airspace during its largest barrage on Ukraine since Sep 7 (593 drones + 50 missiles), Poland and allied jets shot several down and Warsaw halted flights at four airports, and Poland invoked NATO Article 4 (NATO condemned but stopped short of calling it an attack / Article 5); Russia also struck the Poland-Ukraine border area on Sep 13. Combined with Iran again firing ballistic missiles at a US carrier and fresh US strikes in the Gulf, this lifts nuclear_risk_level 0.35->0.37. The 2026 Strait of Hormuz war intensified and widened: US CENTCOM destroyed five IRGC oil tankers, Iran said it attacked ten ships, US aircraft were damaged in a strike on Muwaffaq Salti air base in Jordan, and Houthis seized the Red Sea port of Mokha (second chokepoint re-contested) - Brent crossed $100 for the first time since May on Sep 9 and settled ~$107 on Sep 10 (+~18% on the month). This drives middle_east_stability 0.13->0.12 (war widened to the Red Sea and Jordan; the near-final Iran-Oman shipping-route deal awaiting IMO registration is a partial offset, keeping the slip small), supply_chain_resilience 0.45->0.43 (both Hormuz and Red Sea disrupted, oil at cycle highs), and global_gdp_growth_modifier 1.02->1.01 (a fresh ~$107 oil shock transmits into a growth drag, though equities held near ~7,720 ahead of the Sep 15-16 Fed decision, so only a small tick). Russia-Ukraine ran at record tempo - Ukraine's drone campaign forced an average of ~32 Russian airport closures a day and the Sep 5-8 truce/peace push (Witkoff-Kushner) collapsed without a ceasefire (Zelensky: 'we expect the war will continue') - nudging russia_stability 0.23->0.22; sustained two-front high-intensity combat (record Ukraine barrages, the Gulf tanker war, Red Sea) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,532,500->1,536,500. No new node: the Poland drone incursion, while a serious phase-change in spillover risk, drew Article 4 consultations rather than Article 5 and no NATO-Russia war, so it is scored structurally via nuclear_risk_level and treated as a development within the ongoing Russia-Ukraine and 2026_hormuz_crisis threads, consistent with this log's node discipline (a signed ceasefire or a direct NATO-Russia war would warrant one). Watched but not scored: the Fed's Sep 15-16 decision (even odds hike/hold) falls just outside the window; Super Typhoon Ragasa's Philippines/China landfalls are Sep 22-24 (next window); Copernicus confirmed August was the hottest month on record and the UK banned trade with / sanctioned Israeli West Bank settlements, but neither is a clean structural mover at meaningful magnitude this week; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Sep 10) and GPT Image 2.5 (Sep 8) continued the incremental frontier-AI cadence and do not warrant an ai_development_year_offset tick after the early-September wave already counted; and the Palawan ferry fire and Bangladesh measles outbreak (999 deaths) are regionally acute but not global structural movers.
